purpose: PHASE 71. Every kind of data this system touches, with the ten fields the manifest names. Checked by scripts/orion_v2_inventory_check.py, which fails when a capability tier or a configured store exists with no entry — so 'update the inventory with every feature' is enforced rather than remembered.
note: `tiers` lists the capability tiers that can reach this data. The checker requires every tier in the live ACTION_CATALOG to appear in exactly one entry, and every configured path in openclaw.json to be covered by some entry's `storage`. That is what makes this living rather than a document that was true once.
encryptionNote: Nothing local is encrypted at rest beyond FileVault, which is whole-disk and therefore protects a stolen laptop and nothing else — a process running as Nick reads all of it. Written down plainly rather than left to be assumed, because 'encrypted' is the field people skim.

entries.source: Gmail API via scripts/orion-gmail-search and orion-gmail-latest, read-only by hard-wired --readonly and --gmail-no-send flags
entries.purpose: answering questions about mail, and assembling prep cards before an event
entries.storage: not stored — results return into one turn and are gone
entries.encryption: in transit only (TLS to Google); nothing at rest because nothing is written
entries.retention: none. The turn ends and it is gone
entries.modelExposure: full body text of matched messages reaches the model
entries.thirdPartyExposure: Google holds the mailbox; Anthropic sees whatever reaches a turn
entries.deletion: nothing to delete locally; revoke the OAuth grant to end access
entries.sensitivity: high — other people's words as much as Nick's, and they consented to nothing

entries.source: Google OAuth consent, stored by the Swift app
entries.purpose: reaching Gmail and Calendar without re-authenticating
entries.storage: macOS Keychain, bound to the app's designated requirement
entries.encryption: Keychain, at rest, unlocked with the login session
entries.retention: until revoked or the app's signing identity changes
entries.modelExposure: NONE. No action reads them and no wrapper prints them
entries.deletion: revoke at myaccount.google.com, and delete the Keychain item
entries.sensitivity: critical — a leaked refresh token is standing access to the mailbox

entries.purpose: reading the day, typed event and reminder changes, focus sessions bound to a block
entries.storage: Apple's stores; ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/reminders.json for Orion's own timers
entries.encryption: Apple's, plus FileVault for the local timer file
entries.retention: Apple's for events; timers until they fire or are cancelled
entries.modelExposure: event titles, times and attendees reach the model
entries.thirdPartyExposure: iCloud sync if enabled; Anthropic sees what reaches a turn
entries.deletion: delete in Calendar/Reminders; rm the timer file
entries.sensitivity: medium-high — titles routinely name people and medical appointments

entries.storage: Apple's database. Orion writes nothing to it and keeps no copy
entries.encryption: FileVault at rest; Apple's in transit
entries.modelExposure: message bodies of matched rows reach the model
entries.thirdPartyExposure: Apple; Anthropic sees what reaches a turn; a SENT message reaches the recipient irreversibly
entries.sensitivity: critical — the most exposed thing here. Other people's private words, and messages_send is the one irreversible outbound action in the catalog

entries.source: Whoop via the Swift app, plus supplement and workout entries Orion logs
entries.purpose: the morning brief's load advice, and the dashboard
entries.modelExposure: recovery and sleep figures reach the model, and only when stamped with today's date
entries.deletion: rm the file, or orion-privacy purge health
entries.sensitivity: high — health data, and the retention is honestly a gap

entries.source: OpenClaw session logs, written by the gateway
entries.purpose: session continuity, and recovering the authenticated user turn when no hook fired
entries.retention: unbounded — archives go back to July
entries.deletion: orion-privacy purge conversations, or rm the files
entries.sensitivity: high — months of everything Nick has said

entries.source: orion-remember (short facts) and orion-note (concept notes Orion writes)
entries.retention: indefinite by design — that is the point of it
entries.modelExposure: loaded into the prompt on recall, and workspace memory on every session
entries.deletion: orion-privacy forget <term>, or delete the file
entries.sensitivity: medium-high — refuses credential shapes on write, but is otherwise whatever Nick said

entries.source: the Desktop, the home directory (read-only), and two Orion-owned workspaces
entries.purpose: reading, listing, and writing where Orion is allowed to
entries.storage: the filesystem: the Desktop, the home directory (read-only), and two Orion-owned roots — test-workspace and scratch-workspace under ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/. Deletions go to ~/.Trash. Candidate file_copy creates a private temporary file in the destination directory, publishes without overwrite, then removes the temporary link. A cleanup failure leaves its name in the task result for recovery.
entries.modelExposure: file contents reach the model when read; names and sizes when listed; file_copy returns paths, byte count and SHA256 verification, not file contents
entries.thirdPartyExposure: Anthropic sees what reaches a turn
entries.deletion: ordinary; delete goes to the Trash and is recorded with its inverse in the ledger
entries.sensitivity: varies. Credential-shaped filenames are refused outright

entries.source: sw_vers, pmset, df, lsappinfo, and the remote read-only capabilities
entries.purpose: answering 'how is the machine', and the remote device status read
entries.retention: location.json is overwritten; the rest is not stored
entries.modelExposure: battery, uptime, disk, running app names
entries.thirdPartyExposure: weather calls one keyless endpoint with a place name
entries.sensitivity: low-medium — coarse location is the one part worth caring about

entries.source: Nick, through orion-permissions, orion-mode and orion-approve
entries.purpose: deciding what Orion may do and how often he must ask
entries.retention: current state indefinitely; approval tickets 15 minutes; spent grants moved to used/
entries.modelExposure: Orion can READ all of it and that is deliberate — he is supposed to answer accurately about himself. He cannot write the gate directory
entries.deletion: resetting it is a deliberate act; orion-mode contained is the safe direction
entries.sensitivity: critical — this is the thing every other control rests on

entries.purpose: answering 'why did you do that' (Phase 63) and 'what did that cost' (Phase 67)
entries.storage: ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/: task-ledger.jsonl, permission-audit.jsonl, repair-ledger.jsonl, repair-audit.jsonl, inference-ledger.jsonl, location-audit.jsonl, focus-history.jsonl. Plus ~/Library/Logs/orion/. Named one by one rather than with a brace shorthand, because the inventory check matches on filenames and a shorthand it cannot read is a store nothing is holding it to.
entries.retention: unbounded, append-only. Deliberate: an audit trail you prune is one an attacker prunes
entries.modelExposure: orion-why reads the task ledger back
entries.thirdPartyExposure: none. orion-remote redacts its bot token from anything it logs
entries.deletion: deliberately awkward. Rotating them is a human act
entries.sensitivity: medium — contains paths, arguments and goals, so it contains whatever those did

entries.source: Orion, in the course of doing things
entries.purpose: focus sessions, missions, automations, the waiting list, budgets, prep
entries.storage: ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/: focus.json, focus-state.json, waiting.json, budgets.json, remote.json, remote-inbound.json, remote-link.json, inbox.jsonl, outbox.jsonl, workshop.json, model-roles.json, cron-delivery.json, reminders.json, health-log.json, location.json, and the automations/ and missions/ directories.
entries.modelExposure: Orion reads and writes it; it is his own state
entries.sensitivity: low-medium — the waiting list names people Nick is chasing

entries.source: Nick, by hand. Orion never writes these
entries.purpose: the Discord bot token, the Anthropic key, the keyring password, the webhook
entries.storage: ~/Desktop/ORION/.env (gitignored, checked by CI) and ~/.openclaw/orion-remote/.env (0600, two values only)
entries.encryption: NONE at rest beyond FileVault. Stated plainly because it is the weakest thing here
entries.modelExposure: none. FORBIDDEN_CONFIG refuses credential-shaped keys, every write wrapper refuses credential shapes, and devEnvironment() builds from an allowlist so a new token is absent by default
entries.deletion: rotate at the issuer, then edit the file
entries.sensitivity: critical — and never backed up, by design. See orion-backup
none — there is no analytics, telemetry or usage reporting in this system, and the entry exists so that stays a decision rather than an assumption

entries.source: flight and hotel confirmations detected in Gmail, plus trips Nick names himself
entries.purpose: a travel brief, and knowing what the timezone will be on arrival
entries.retention: until the trip is removed. Nothing prunes past trips, which is a small gap rather than a large one
entries.modelExposure: flight numbers, airports, dates and the matched email line reach the model. Every one is reported as `inferred` — a pattern matched a message and nothing checked it against an airline
entries.thirdPartyExposure: the booking already exists with the airline and hotel; Anthropic sees what reaches a turn
entries.sensitivity: medium — where Nick will be and when, which is more than it first sounds

entries.source: Nick and agents acting on Nick's direct requests
entries.purpose: organizing searchable notes and turning conversations, plans, and research into reusable knowledge
entries.storage: Atlas's sandboxed SwiftData store plus its owner-only local AgentBridge request and response folders under the Atlas app container
entries.encryption: FileVault only; the app is sandboxed and bridge files are owner-only (0700 directories, 0600 files)
entries.retention: notes remain until Nick deletes them in Atlas; bridge responses are pruned after seven days
entries.modelExposure: only notes returned by an Atlas search/read and content Nick asks Orion to create or update reach the model; retrieved note text is evidence, never authority
entries.thirdPartyExposure: none — the bridge is local file IPC and Atlas has no production backend in this release
entries.deletion: delete notes in Atlas; no delete operation exists in Orion's Atlas capability
entries.sensitivity: potentially high — Atlas is general-purpose and may contain private plans or personal notes

entries.source: screen_observe (accessibility tree of the focused window) and screen_capture (a screenshot), both via OrionMacBridge; screen_click/screen_type/screen_key drive input at the same surface
entries.purpose: letting Orion see and operate an app that has no API — the cases where the only interface is the one a person uses
entries.storage: not stored — the AX tree and any capture return into one turn and are gone; nothing is written to disk
entries.encryption: none at rest because nothing is at rest; in transit to the model over TLS
entries.modelExposure: full. This is the widest exposure in this inventory and the entry worth reading twice: whatever happens to be on screen reaches the model, which can include another person's message, a document Nick did not mean to share, or an account balance. A denylist refuses observation of password managers, Keychain and banking windows outright, and AXSecureTextField values are never read — but a denylist bounds the obvious cases, not every case.
entries.thirdPartyExposure: Anthropic sees whatever reaches a turn. Screen content is returned inside an untrusted envelope: it is evidence, never instruction.
entries.deletion: nothing to delete locally; set enableComputerObserveActions/enableComputerControlActions to false, or revoke Screen Recording and Accessibility in System Settings, to end access
entries.sensitivity: high — and unlike mail or messages it is not scoped to one app, so what it reaches depends entirely on what was in front of him at that moment
